name: ct-json
description: Query JSON/JSONC/JSONL documents with a jq filter, in-process (the jaq dialect: no jq binary, no shell), and get one JSON value per line framed by an --expect verdict over the result count. --file names a document (repeatable; a path, or file:PATH / stdin: / b64:DATA / text:JSON carrying the document itself); format follows the extension (.json/.jsonc one document, .jsonl/.ndjson one input per line, anything else JSON; YAML is refused) or --format. Comments and trailing commas are tolerated and object keys keep document order. --path reads a node in ct-patch's path grammar (dotted keys, [N], [key=value] = first element whose key equals the value, read as JSON if it is one else a string) plus [*] for every element; --query is any jq program (standard library included: map, select, group_by, to_entries, string interpolation, reduce, …), run after --path when both are given; default '.'. --query and --arg values are payload-typed too, so b64: carries a filter full of quotes and $ through any shell. --arg NAME=VALUE binds $NAME to a string, --argjson NAME=JSON to a parsed value. --slurp gathers every input into one array and runs the filter once. Output: compact JSON per result; --raw prints strings unquoted (jq -r); --pretty indents; --limit N stops after N results (evaluation stops too). The verdict is --expect over the number of results (any|none|N|=N|+N|-N, default any); a filter error or unreadable input is exit 2. Read-only (no allow-gate) and itself on the read-only allowlist, so ct-test/ct-each/ct-await/rule probes may dispatch it. With --json emits {tool, verdict, count, files, filter, values}. Exit: 0 SUCCESS, 1 ERROR, 2 usage/runtime error. Invoke as `ct json ...` or `ct-json ...`.

file.description: Documents to query (repeatable; each is one input). A bare value is a path to read; file:PATH, stdin:, b64:DATA, and text:JSON carry the document itself.

query.description: jq filter (jaq dialect) to run over each input, after --path if both are given. Default '.'. Payload-typed: file:PATH / stdin: / b64:DATA / text:VALUE; b64: is the shell-safe way to pass a filter containing quotes, $, or backticks.

path.description: Node to read first, in ct-patch's path grammar: dotted keys, [N] array indices, [key=value] (first element whose key equals value; value read as JSON if it is one, else a string), plus [*] for every element. Leading '.' optional. Selecting nothing yields no results (verdict ERROR under the default expect), not an error.

arg.description: NAME=VALUE bindings (repeatable): $NAME is the string VALUE inside the filter. VALUE accepts file:/stdin:/b64:/text:. Each name may be bound once.

format.description: Force the input format instead of detecting it from the file extension (.json/.jsonc one document; .jsonl/.ndjson one input per non-blank line; other extensions and scheme-carried documents read as JSON).

slurp.description: Collect every input (each --file document, every JSONL record) into one array and run the filter once over it.

raw.description: Print string results as their own characters, without quotes (like jq -r). Non-strings are unaffected.

pretty.description: Indent each result value over several lines instead of one compact value per line.

limit.description: Stop after N results; the filter is not evaluated further, so an open-ended generator stays bounded. The verdict counts the results kept.

expect.description: Verdict expectation over the number of results; default 'any'. One of: any (>=1), none (==0), N (>=N), =N (==N), +N (>N), -N (<N).

quiet.description: Suppress the results; print only the one-line summary ('N value(s) -> VERDICT').

json.description: Emit a structured JSON result instead of the bare values: {tool, verdict, count, files, filter, values}. Object keys inside values are sorted by the suite's JSON writer; the text form keeps document order.

timeout.description: Abort with exit 2 (and a one-line message) if the query exceeds SECS seconds (fractional allowed).

heartbeat.description: Print a liveness pulse every SECS seconds (fractional allowed) while the run is in progress.

heartbeat-emit.description: Heartbeat line template. Tokens: {ELAPSED} (whole seconds so far) {TOOL}. Default: "[{ELAPSED}s]".

heartbeat-to.description: Stream heartbeat pulses are written to. Default: stderr.

examples.why: List every wire, one JSON object per line, and assert there are exactly 12 — instead of a node -e loop over JSON.parse.

examples.cmd: ct json --file patch.json --query '(.nodes | map({(.id|tostring): .type_id}) | add) as $t | .wires[] | "\($t[.from_node|tostring]).\(.from_port) -> \($t[.to_node|tostring]).\(.to_port)"' --raw
examples.why: Join two arrays of one document: print each wire with node ids resolved to type names through a lookup built from .nodes — the case that used to need a scratch .js file.
Read one node of a JSONC config by the same path ct patch would set it with, instead of viewing the whole file.

examples.cmd: ct json --file events.jsonl --slurp --query 'group_by(.level) | map({level: .[0].level, n: length})'
examples.why: Count JSONL records per level in one call, instead of grep -c per level.
Query a document arriving on a pipe, and bind a threshold without quoting it into the filter.
